main_text.p: tuū intellígi, quo captiuus abductus est:Ergo siue nepote illo emancipato ante testatorem mortuo, siue etiam & filio captiuo, & ipso nepote uiuìs, post mortē aui testatoris aliquis nascatur, nequaquā testamentū rūpet. Nec ad rē attinebat quærere, Quare nō indu xere formulā quæ huic casuì accōmo-data essèt? quasi uerò Galli formula non huic casui uel maximè consenta-nea sit: modò pro uoce NEPOS, suppo namus PRONEPOS.' Quod autem Ceruidius adscribit, Nam hic casus ad legem Velleā non pertinet: iis adscri-psisse uidetur, qui dubitare possent, u-trū de Gallo Aquilio, an de gallo gal-linaceo hæc intellīgēda sint. Age, reli qua consideremus. nunc enim tandē Ceruidius nos longa & molesta nauí-gatione iactatos, ad portum perducit. Docuit superius quàm imperfecta & manca Galli Aquilij formula sibi uide retur: nunc alteram nobis à se affabrè atq; antiquo artificio factam profert.
Et melius ergo est, inquit, ut in huiusmodi utilitates, id est, cum istiusmodi casus inciderirint, qui postumi institu-tionem

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "tuū" at the start of the first line is read as printed but is hard to make out. "indu xere" and "uide retur" are printed with a space inside the word and are kept as printed. "Ceruidius" and "PRONEPOS" are as printed. The stray mark before "Ceruidius" on the left edge and the show-through are not transcribed. The text stops mid-sentence at the foot of the page, so the last line is the continuation of "institu-tionem" with its printed hyphen.
